messages.content: Predict a human allocation in the initial generic dictator game of an online experiment. The dictator alone chooses an offer to another person, called the recipient; the recipient has no action and cannot accept, reject or alter the offer. This is the generic baseline recipient without an emotional facial-expression cue, before the series of face trials. Do not invent a recipient photograph, appearance, emotion, needs or prior behavior. The task uses hypothetical euros; allocations do not produce real cash rewards. Course credit or uncompensated participation is separate from the hypothetical offer. Participants were told that this was part of a larger project and that offers were being prepared for people who had played a similar game previously and provided photos. This statement does not supply the recipient's prior actions. The paper reports the dictator-game offer slider as EUR 0–10. Its original initial generic screen and a separately stated total endowment are unavailable, so do not infer an additional payment, an initial wealth or that the dictator keeps 10 minus the offer. Predict the euro amount GIVEN to the recipient, not the amount kept, an emotion label, a fraction or A/B. Original interface increments are not established; do not assume that only integer options were available. Demographic and German SPF(IRI) empathy questionnaires preceded this initial game. The supplied individual profile comes from that same source record, with no outcome-based cross-file identity match. Age is in years. Gender uses the source categories female, male or diverse; diverse is not recoded as male. The four original pretask empathy subscale scores are on the reported 1–5 score metric, four items per subscale: SPF_FS (fantasy) concerns identification with fictional characters, SPF_EC (empathic concern) concern/sympathy for others, SPF_PT (perspective taking) consideration of others' viewpoints, and SPF_PD (personal distress) one's own distress in tense interpersonal situations. These are reported subscale scores rather than individual item answers, diagnoses, probabilities or percentages. Higher scores indicate a greater tendency of the named construct; personal distress is not automatically prosocial concern. No current or later allocation, emotion-specific mean, emotional index, standardized cohort score, rating or recipient feedback is provided. The later face trials have not occurred at this initial event; do not invent their history. Output only the amount offered in euros as a number, without a unit or explanation.
